item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-25 23:59
Institution: Univ. PALERMO, Palermo
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

This position is funded by the ERC Starting Grant REFINE2LASE recipient Prof. Emanuele Marino and is part of Work Package 2, which aims to understand the physical mechanisms underlying the thermal refinement of colloidal nanocrystals. The research will involve developing coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations informed by experimental small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) data to study superlattice nucleation and growth and nanocrystal size selection. These simulations will help identify efficient thermal protocols to obtain nanocrystal populations with reduced polydispersity for use in the microlasers envisioned by the project. item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Characterizing the dynamics of innovation in human activities and biological systems (ROMA "La Sapienza")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-12-09 23:59
Institution: ROMA "La Sapienza", Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-04 Fisica teorica della materia, modelli, metodi matematici e applicazioni

Innovations and novelties concern, at a fundamental level, human activities, social behaviours, and biological systems. The vast majority of these systems are intrinsically open systems: new, previously unknown elements may continuously emerge. Statistical and dynamical regularities are shared by systems featuring innovation, pointing to general, i.e., non-system-specific, mechanisms underlying the innovation process. We will deepen the study of a class of Pólya-urn-based models that reproduce many of the empirical behaviours observed in real-world systems, while searching for novel relevant observables to characterise the latter.

Global climate models fail to capture local phenomena due to their coarse spatial resolution—resolution that is nonetheless essential for assessing micro-scale climate change impacts, such as urban heat islands and pollutant dispersion. The research project aims to develop and optimize advanced numerical techniques for dynamic downscaling by integrating fluid dynamics data (LES/DNS) with mesoscale models (WRF). item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Higgs precision measurements at the LHC and at the future circular colllider (Univ. BARI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-14 23:55
Institution: Univ. BARI, Roma
Field: Physics / 02/PHYS-01 Fisica sperimentale delle interazioni fondamentali e applicazioni

The research project aims, first, to develop data analysis techniques for measuring the trilinear coupling of the Higgs boson with itself, which would provide an important test of the Higgs mechanism by determining the shape of the Higgs potential. Experimentally, this coupling can be extracted by measuring the non-resonant production cross section of Higgs boson (HH) pairs at the LHC and the future circular collider, currently under preparation at CERN. Specifically, the project intends to study the production of double Higgs in final states with a pair of b-jets and charged leptons using advanced machine learning techniques, by using data collected by the CMS experiment.
